facts.raw_span: 61-year-old woman with type II diabetes
several days of urinary retention
1-year history of progressive lower-extremity weakness
100-lb unintentional weight loss
bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles
atrophy of the hands and thighs
sensation to light touch was reduced in the feet
reflexes were 2+ in the upper extremities and absent at the knees and ankles
bladder catheterization yielded 1.8 L of retained urine
CSF analysis revealed protein 175 mg/dL
electromyography and nerve conduction studies demonstrated decreased amplitudes in motor and sensory nerves
MRI of the pelvis showed bilateral femoral nerve enlargement without enhancement

concepts.why: The patient's progressive lower-extremity weakness, bilateral weakness of multiple muscle groups, reduced sensation, and absent reflexes in the lower extremities, along with elevated CSF protein and abnormal electromyography and nerve conduction studies, are consistent with CIDP.

rationales.F03: Progressive lower-extremity weakness is a key feature of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy and lumbosacral plexopathy.
rationales.F05: Bilateral weakness of hip flexors, knee flexors, knee extensors, and intrinsic hand muscles is consistent with a demyelinating polyneuropathy.
rationales.F08: Absent reflexes at the knees and ankles are a characteristic finding in chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.
rationales.F10: Elevated CSF protein is a hallmark of chronic inflammatory demyelinating polyneuropathy.
rationales.F11: Electromyography and nerve conduction studies demonstrating decreased amplitudes and slowed conduction velocities are consistent with a demyelinating polyneuropathy.
rationales.F12: Bilateral femoral nerve enlargement without enhancement on MRI is consistent with lumbosacral plexopathy.
